Hi all,

Thanks for the call earlier — per request, attaching a concise runbook for how Redwood plans to (1) emit usage records to AWS Marketplace metering; (2) surface entitlement proof for license-based SKUs; and (3) reconcile monthly billing with ACME finance.

Attached: initial connector spec (redwood_aws_billing_connector_v1.pdf) and a mapping draft.

Next steps we propose:
- AWS: confirm metering dimension and ingestion window (within 24 hours?).
- ACME procurement: confirm required fields for license proof (company legal name, account id, seat counts).
- Redwood (Ben/Marcus): finalize mapping and produce the sample payload for test ingestion by Friday.

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: SaaS billing connector & license verification runbook

Evelyn/Team,

Thanks for the summary and the doc. Quick answers from the Marketplace side:

- Metering dimension: for SaaS contracts we prefer a single numeric "usage_quantity" per hour (UTC) tied to the customer entitlement id. Aggregation by day is acceptable if you ensure idempotency on replays.
- Ingestion window: usage reports are accepted up to 24 hours after the interval; beyond that you must use the "correction" flow and include previous report ids.
- Entitlement proof: we accept a signed JWT that contains the entitlement key + expiration, accompanied by a CSV with customer account mapping. The CSV should include columns: aws_customer_id, redwood_account_id, sku_id, entitlement_start, entitlement_end, seats.

Two operational notes:
1) Please throttle to avoid >200 requests/min per account during test ingestion.
2) For license SKUs, include a static "license_proof_id" in the usage payload so we can tie usage to active entitlement records.

If you can send a sample payload (JSON + signed JWT) to mp-integ@amazonaws.com we'll run a dry ingestion in our staging environment.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Ops
---
Note: this mailbox monitors ingestion errors; include correlation-id in the subject for follow-ups.

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: SaaS billing connector & license verification runbook

Thanks — useful clarifications. A couple of ACME-specific questions (looping in Marcus for mapping):

- ACME has both seat-based and consumption-based seats internally. For seat SKUs, do you want us to emit a constant hourly quantity of the active seat_count, or a once-per-day snapshot? ACME prefers hourly to avoid large correction windows.
- For the signed JWT: does AWS require an external CA signature, or is an internal Redwood-signed JWS (RS256) with a public key we publish to S3 sufficient?

ACME procurement: can you confirm the exact column names your invoicing system needs — we want to avoid back-and-forth on CSV headers during go-live.

Ben
Sr. Sales Engineer, Marketplaces
Redwood Inference

Folks,

I've sketched the mapping and a payload template and attached the workbook. Key decisions:
- Seat SKUs: we'll emit an hourly usage_quantity equal to active_seats (resolved against ACME's license API). This keeps corrections small and aligns with AWS ingestion windows.
- Consumption SKUs: emit actual token units / 1000 to keep the numeric range within integer limits on AWS. We'll include a "unit_scale": 1000 in the payload metadata.
- JWT: Redwood will sign JWS (RS256). We'll publish the public key to a time-versioned S3 path and include the s3_url in the JWT header per AWS suggestion.

Attachments: license-proof-mapping.xlsx (contains the CSV column set and sample rows).

I can export a one-off sample payload (JSON + signed JWT) by EOD and send to mp-integ@amazonaws.com for staging ingestion.

Marcus Lin
Principal Integrations Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: AWS Marketplace: SaaS billing connector & license verification runbook — consolidated next steps

ACME / AWS team,

Thanks for the quick responses. Summary and agreed next steps below (consolidated):

1) Metering model
- Seat SKUs: hourly usage_quantity = active_seats. Redwood will call ACME license API each hour and emit usage.
- Consumption SKUs: usage reported in token-thousands (unit_scale=1000).

2) Entitlement proof
- Redwood will generate RS256-signed JWTs. Public key will be published to s3://redwood-attachments/acme/keys/v1.pub. JWT + CSV (columns: aws_customer_id, redwood_account_id, sku_id, entitlement_start, entitlement_end, seats, license_proof_id) will be sent as the proof bundle.

3) Ingestion & testing
- Redwood to send a sample payload (JSON + signed JWT) to mp-integ@amazonaws.com by EOD Nov 26.
- AWS to run a dry ingestion and return any validation errors with a correlation id.

4) Go-live criteria
- Successful dry ingestion + zero validation errors for a 48-hour window in staging.
- Signed DocuSign amendment to the SaaS contract for marketplace billing (link below).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/RDW-ACME-SaaS-2026
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/89012

I've attached the integration checklist as CSV for ACME's procurement and finance teams. Marcus/Bob (ACME), if the headers look correct please confirm and we'll generate the first payload.

Best,
